title: Court registers for the people and organizations in existing cases
question: What do the Superior Court registers show now for the criminal and civil cases the existing cases cite?
finding: A grand jury indictment was filed on 2025-11-18 (case CRI-25025111) naming Stanley Ellicott with Lanita Henriquez (#25023975) and Dwayne Jones (#25024194) as co-defendants; bail on the 2023 complaints was exonerated on 2025-11-19 (Jones) and 2025-11-20 (Henriquez). Ellicott's 2024 case shows orders paying restitution from frozen accounts at Axos, Fidelity, Green Dot Bank, Patelco Credit Union, Voya Financial (latest 2026-02-19) and an abstract of judgment filed 2026-02-23. Westbrook's register shows 4 entries "preliminary hearing ... not waived" (2026-03-09, 2026-04-17, 2026-07-29, 2026-10-21) and no plea; Davis's and Spingola's last minute orders are dated 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-13; the two Providence defendants' last minute orders are dated 2026-11-03. In the City's suit against the Santos firm, an amended judgment after trial was entered on 2026-01-28, the City was awarded attorney fees, the remaining property-owner defendant appealed (A175716), and an abstract of judgment issued to the City on 2026-07-31. The City Attorney's writ petition against the Controller's hearing officer (Collective Impact) was filed 2025-12-24; the real party was served on 2026-07-30, and no hearing or ruling appears.
how: Each register exported from the court's case-information site is read entry by entry (date and proceeding). Key entries are picked by their wording (indictment, plea, judgment, restitution, appeal, preliminary-hearing waivers); "hearings" counts minute orders.
limits: A register lists filings, not their content: it does not give charges, counts, sentences or amounts, and a minute order can be a continuance. Everyone charged is presumed innocent; Henriquez, Jones, Westbrook, Davis, Spingola and the two Providence staffers have not been convicted. Private parties in the civil case are not named.
